problem: Visual-navigation RL agents learn weak visual representations that don't jointly capture object semantics, spatial location, and temporal causality between actions and observation changes.
motivation: The mapping from observation to visual representation determines the navigation policy. Fusing local and global visual information with temporal sequence modeling should help the agent reach the target object more effectively.
key_idea: Use a spatial attention probability fused model (SAF) together with a sequential transformer (STNet) that imagines next observations and infers actions, conditioned autoregressively on reward, past states, actions and a knowledge graph.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that combining inter-image spatial cues (SAF) with intra-image sequential decoding (STNet) lets the agent learn the causality between actions and observation changes.
method: SAF (spatial attention probability fused model): fuses cross-modal state into visual clues, encoding object semantics and their spatial locations to exploit image inter-relations.
STNet (sequential transformer network): generates (imagines) the next observations and infers actions focused on the aspects most relevant to the target, decoding image intra-relations.
Autoregressive conditioning: SSTNet is conditioned on desired reward, past states, actions and a knowledge graph, in a decision-transformer-like way.
DRL training: the visual representation is learned within a deep reinforcement learning framework.

setting.backbone: SSTNet (SAF + STNet transformer), trained with deep RL

setting.action_space: discrete navigation actions (not detailed in abstract)
